title: control-plane-archive-and-index-rewrite
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Reduce control plane query latency and storage costs by partitioning the largest time-series tables, moving cold rows to an archival store, and replacing several high-cardinality scans with expression/partial indexes. This ticket standardizes the migration pattern and performs an online reindex without extended downtime.
background: Recent production incidents surfaced long-running queries against control_plane.events and control_plane.audit_log during tenant listing and connection churn windows.
Growth of audit_log JSON payloads and unbounded append behavior has led to table bloat and p99 query regressions for admin read APIs.
Previous ad-hoc indexes mitigated some hotpaths but several queries still do sequential scans because of wide predicate shapes and non-sargable JSON conditions.
acceptance_criteria: control_plane.audit_log is partitioned by month with a transparent partition pruning strategy and automated retention policy
Cold partitions older than 90 days are archived to S3 (Parquet) and retrievable via a read-path that streams results for audit exports
Top-10 slow queries in control plane dashboards show median latency improvement >= 40% and p99 improvement >= 30% in canary cluster
Online reindex executed with pg_repack (or equivalent) completing without >5% increase in read-latency during the migration window
Data integrity validated between active partitions and archival store (checksums and sample row counts)
New partial/expression indexes reduce seq-scans for tenant_lookup and route resolution queries (verified by EXPLAIN ANALYZE)
Change is covered by a runbook: prechecks, rollback steps, and smoke-tests documented in Confluence
technical_approach: Audit and baseline: capture EXPLAIN ANALYZE for top 25 slowest queries across control_plane schema and identify candidate tables (audit_log, events, tenant_metadata)
Design partitions: use monthly RANGE partitioning on created_at for audit_log; smaller retention window for events with BRIN index on created_at for older partitions
Index rewrite: add expression indexes for ( (payload->>'tenant_id')::uuid ) and partial indexes for active_status = 'open' to cover the hottest predicates
Online ops: employ pg_repack for live reindexing and CLUSTER less-critical tables during low-traffic windows; schedule canary on staging -> canary-prod cluster before fleet-wide rollout

Archival: background worker that exports older partitions to S3 in compressed Parquet, registers manifests for retrieval; query-layer implements transparent fallback to fetch archived rows when needed
Migration automation: add idempotent SQL migration scripts and a lightweight orchestrator job that runs prechecks, applies partition creation, migrates ranges, and runs consistency checks
Monitoring: extend console dashboard to track migration progress, partition sizes, pg_stat_activity stalls, and IO spikes. Add alerts for long-running COPY/EXPORT jobs.
rollout_plan: 1) Baseline collection: 48h capture of query plans and production load
2) Staging run: execute full migration workflow against production snapshot in staging cluster; validate runbook
3) Canary: apply to 10% of prod control-plane traffic (canary cluster) during off-peak; run pg_repack on single partition
4) Gradual partitioning: create new monthly partitions in prod, move 30/60/90+ day data into partitions in waves
5) Archive sweep: export oldest partitions to S3; verify retrieval path
6) Index add/remove: add new expression/partial indexes, monitor hit rates; drop legacy wide indexes after 7 days of stable metrics
7) Post-migration: run full integrity checks and update docs and dashboards; schedule follow-up 2-week check-in
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: EXPORT jobs saturate IO causing increased API latencies -> Mitigation: throttle exports, run during low-traffic windows, use parallelism cap
Risk: pg_repack causes bloat or long locks on older Postgres versions -> Mitigation: test on staging with same minor version, fall back to reindex concurrently where available
Risk: mismatch between archived Parquet schema and production -> Mitigation: enforce schema evolution guardrails and include row-level checksums
Risk: queries still hit legacy joins -> Mitigation: run EXPLAIN on production after each index change and add query-level hints to route to new indexes if required
notes: Spike found that JSONB->> extraction is non-sargable in several queries; casting to typed columns or indexed expressions drastically improves plans
We will coordinate with infra for maintenance windows and request temporary elevated IO budget from cloud provider during migration
This ticket intentionally avoids a full Postgres major upgrade; a follow-up ticket will handle pg13->pg15 after partitioning is stable
